maya: @infra-bot popped an alert for gpu-card-34 — ECC spike (120/min) + a few Xid(43) in last 8m. Did the autodrain kick?

infra-bot: hw-health-hook: soft-cordon applied to node gpu-node-123 (reason: ECC rate high). Drift-state=soft -> waiting 10m hold before hard-evict. EventID=E20240315-998

sanjay: link to runbook? is this path using k8s drain or slurm deactivation first?

maya: runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-health (TL;DR: soft-cordon -> try hw-reset -> if PCIe resets > 5 or repeat Xid -> hard drain and slurm deact). We recently lowered hold to 10m for faster recovery, maybe too aggressive.

leah: can we failover to a warm spare-pool (eu-central1) before hard-drain? that avoids queued job churn. cost tradeoff if we keep spares warm though.

devendra: proposal: require 2 signals within window OR signal + PCIe reset burst before full drain. Pseudocode:

``
if ECC_rate > ECC_THRESH and (PCIe_resets > 5 or recent_Xid_count > 3):
  escalate_to_hard_drain()
else:
  soft_cordon_hold(minutes=15)
  attempt_hw_reset()
```

this reduces noisy single-spike drains.

ori-bot: note: k8s taint + slurm controlcmd must be ordered: slurm node set state=DRAIN before k8s eviction to avoid job overlap. drain-mode=soft -> hard -> reimage is our canonical flow.

sanjay: what's the cost hit for 10 warm spares in prod?

maya: rough calc: 10 DGX-like spares ~ +3.2% monthly infra spend for prod cluster. With autoscaler we can convert preemptible capacity to spares cheaper, but availability variance.

devendra: another option: staggered fallback — soft-cordon triggers preemptible takeover of low-priority jobs, only spin warm spares if preemptible insufficient. Autoscaler hook would need a 2-step: preemptible->warm->reimage.

infra-bot: update: node gpu-node-123 attempted hw-reset (pci-reset cmd) — 1 reset so far. still soft-cordoned. Will re-evaluate at 1719124100.

leah: ok, +1 to adding PCIe-reset count into the gating. can someone draft a small RFC for the gating thresholds and spare-pool policy?

maya: I'll draft RFC and post in #eng-infra later today. :thumbsup:
